planting.note: Plant dormant canes or containerized plants in early spring; floricanes bear fruit in their second year, so expect a light or no crop the first season.

directions: Ervin is a thornless, floricane-fruiting blackberry from the North Carolina State University caneberry breeding program, named for longtime cooperating grower Ervin Lineberger. It follows the program's earlier release 'Von' and is notable for unusually high sugar content, giving the glossy black fruit a markedly sweet, dessert-quality flavor compared with older commercial cultivars. Canes are vigorous and benefit from trellising to support fruit weight and ease harvest. Remove spent floricanes after harvest and thin new primocanes to keep the row open and fruit size large.
sources: NC State University College of Agriculture and Life Sciences news
NC State Extension caneberry breeding program

planting.note: Plant dormant canes in early spring on a trellis or support wires; Glen Dee is a late-ripening floricane type suited to fresh-market and tunnel production.

directions: Glen Dee is a late-season red raspberry from the James Hutton Institute's Scottish breeding program (successor to the Scottish Crop Research Institute), part of the spine-free 'Glen' series developed for fresh-market and protected cropping. Fruit is sweet-tart with a firm texture that holds up well for shipping, carried on upright, completely spine-free primocanes. The cultivar carries the A10 resistance gene against the large raspberry aphid along with field tolerance to root rot. Train canes to a support wire and remove spent floricanes after harvest to keep rows productive.
sources: U.S. Plant Patent USPP27660 — Rubus plant named 'Glen Dee'

planting.note: Plant dormant canes in early spring on support wires; bred for fresh-market and protected (tunnel) cropping.

directions: Glen Carron is a red raspberry from the James Hutton Institute's spine-free 'Glen' breeding series, selected for fresh-market and protected cropping. Fruit is bright red and conical, with a very sweet flavor and notably low acidity, and the berries are easy to pick cleanly from the receptacle. Canes are upright and free of prickles, simplifying both training and harvest labor. Support canes on wires and remove spent floricanes after fruiting to maintain vigor in the next season's primocanes.
sources: Frank P Matthews nursery catalogue — Glen Carron Raspberry

planting.note: Plant dormant canes in early spring on a trellis; a summer-fruiting floricane type released from the same Scottish breeding program cross that produced 'Glen Ample'.

directions: Glen Rosa is a red raspberry released in the mid-1990s from the Scottish Crop Research Institute (now the James Hutton Institute) breeding program, a sister seedling from the same cross that produced 'Glen Ample'. It carries the A10 resistance gene against the large raspberry aphid, making it useful where aphid-vectored virus pressure is a concern, though its berries and yields run smaller than its sibling. Canes are spine-free and upright, typical of the 'Glen' series bred for ease of picking. Train to support wires and remove fruited floricanes after harvest to favor new primocane growth.
sources: Scottish Crop Research Institute raspberry breeding trial reports

planting.note: Plant dormant canes in early spring; a primocane (fall-bearing) type that can also be mowed to the ground each winter for a single late-season crop.

directions: Crimson Treasure is a fall-bearing (primocane) red raspberry from Cornell AgriTech's berry breeding program in Geneva, New York, the third release in Cornell's 'Crimson' raspberry series after 'Crimson Giant' and 'Crimson Night'. Its standout trait is fruit size nearly double that of the long-standard 'Heritage', and the berries hold their bright red color and firm texture in storage rather than darkening and softening. The plant is very high yielding and has shown broad adaptability in trials well beyond New York. For a single fall crop, mow all canes to the ground in late winter; for an earlier or extended harvest, retain some canes to also fruit as floricanes the following summer.
sources: Cornell University news — new high-yield strawberry, raspberry varieties released

planting.note: Plant dormant canes or divisions in early spring; a cold-hardy primocane type bred for short-season northern climates.

directions: Redwing is a fall-bearing (primocane) red raspberry released in 1988 by the University of Minnesota fruit breeding program, bred for exceptional winter hardiness in short-season northern climates where many fall-bearing cultivars fail to ripen a full crop. Fruit is medium-sized and ripens notably earlier than the standard 'Heritage', typically ten to fourteen days ahead, which lets gardeners in cold regions harvest a reliable crop before frost ends the season. Plants are compact and can be mowed to the ground each winter for a straightforward single fall harvest the following year. Give full sun and even moisture through fruit set for best berry size.
sources: University of Minnesota fruit breeding program — raspberry cultivar records
University of Minnesota Extension — raspberries for the home garden
